nodes.name: Webhook
nodes.notes:
POST from /api/admin/action. The app already checked the session and
stamped `actor` — that is what the audit row is written from.

nodes.name: Which action?
nodes.notes:
One Switch. The audit insert sits AFTER it, on the shared path — that is
the entire reason there is a single write endpoint.

parameters.jsCode:
return [{ json: { payload: { contribution_id: $('Webhook').first().json.body.id,
  status: 'approved', actor: $('Webhook').first().json.body.actor } } }];

const b = $('Webhook').first().json.body;
return [{ json: { payload: { contribution_id: b.id, status: 'rejected', actor: b.actor } } }];

const b = $('Webhook').first().json.body;
return [{ json: { payload: { nomination_id: b.id, status: 'approved', actor: b.actor } } }];

const b = $('Webhook').first().json.body;
return [{ json: { payload: { nomination_id: b.id, status: 'rejected', actor: b.actor } } }];

const b = $('Webhook').first().json.body;
return [{ json: { payload: { contribution_id: b.id, patch: b.patch, actor: b.actor } } }];

const b = $('Webhook').first().json.body;
return [{ json: { payload: { person_id: b.id, body: b.body, actor: b.actor } } }];

parameters.jsonBody:
={{ JSON.stringify({ payload: { actor: $('Webhook').first().json.body.actor,
  action: $('Webhook').first().json.body.action,
  resource: 'admin', resource_id: $('Webhook').first().json.body.id ?? null,
  after: $('Webhook').first().json.body } }) }}

nodes.name: Write the audit row
nodes.notes:
On the shared path, not inside each branch. Most setters write their
own row as well; this one catches the action itself, including the
ones that only change state through a page.

parameters.jsCode:
return [{ json: { ok: true, persisted: true,
  actor: $('Webhook').first().json.body.actor } }];
